source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Structural and Family-level Features in BiRNA-BERT
source.authors: M. Hossain; MD. Roqunuzzaman Sojib; Md Toki Tahmid; M. S. Rahman

page_placements.theme: Downstream utility depends on task and comparison baseline

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE features recover biological signals in an RNA language model, a new model and biological setting; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The study measures biological associations of SAE features in BiRNA-BERT. It does not test whether features overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, the capacity-pressure account of polysemanticity, or the dimensionality of the underlying features. Reported results from cited work and hyperparameter choices are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on a frozen RNA language model (BiRNA-BERT) and measures whether SAE features align with biological labels. That bears on V4: whether a real model contains sparse features a dictionary can recover, in a new domain. It does not test toy-model geometry, capacity accounts, canonicity of features, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs expose biological structure in BiRNA-BERT while preserving model behaviour. They find mean structural enrichment is largest at the middle layer. Sparse profiles modestly improve kNN balanced accuracy over dense embeddings and stay ahead of length/composition baselines, and sequence length must be controlled for.
record.recipe_differences: Layer-wise SAEs trained on a frozen RNA language model, followed by biological feature-alignment analyses; not the original toy-network feature-superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by layer: structural enrichment is highest at layer 5; SAE kNN performance improves over dense embeddings at layers 5 and 11 but declines at layer 0. RNA-type effect sizes are controlled for sequence length.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-profile kNN RNA-type accuracy beats dense embeddings at layers 5 and 11 (0.359 vs 0.328; 0.284 vs 0.275) but not at layer 0. A length+composition baseline reaches 0.298.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The representational utility of SAE profiles for RNA-type classification varies by layer and is partly explained by sequence length and composition.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA of layer-5 dense and SAE profiles shows overlapping RNA types, with silhouette −0.197 for both, and leading components correlated with sequence length (|r| up to 0.74).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-dimensional organization of these RNA representations largely reflects sequence length.

record.problems: The evidence concerns one frozen RNA language model and three analyzed layers. RNA-type classes are strongly imbalanced, typical length-controlled feature effects are small, and the authors report length confounding in pooled profiles and PCA. No confidence intervals or error bars are stated for the reported aggregate metrics.
record.rows_left_out: No additional main-text results bearing directly on the tested claim version were omitted. Individual per-type confusion-matrix values and supplementary analyses are not separately cataloged because they measure classification behavior rather than SAE feature recoverability.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, no geometry, no sparsity transition.
All of it: no capacity or importance analysis.
All of it: no analysis of the origins of polysemanticity.
Spreading of features across neurons. Only one non-LLM RNA model and three layers are tested.
Completeness, stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, and canonicity of SAE features. Only one dictionary size (6,144) is used.
Whether the features are 1-D or multi-dimensional.

missing.what: Reconstruction fidelity (EV >0.99997, KL ~1e-5) and mean L0 of 975/775/791 active features per token (15.9/12.6/12.9%). These exceed the 768-dimensional hidden size and bear on how sparse the recovered features are.

Stem dominance of significant features: 5,862 of 5,988 at layer 0. Also peak per-feature enrichment (F563 Bulge 26.9× at layer 5; 19.5× and 20.0× at layers 0 and 11) and perfectly selective layer-5 features absent at layer 0.

record.verdict_notes: The test of V4 is indirect: biological alignment of SAE features in one RNA model. The SAE is not actually very sparse (L0 > d_model), which weakens any reading as recovery of sparse superposed features. The original (Toy Models) is cited only as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric arrangements.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or causes important features to receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Does not test feature spreading across neurons; tests SAE-feature associations in one RNA language model, not a range of LLMs.
Does not establish SAE features as complete, stable, canonical units; cross-layer feature matching is not a test of completeness or stability.
Does not test whether the model’s represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: SAE sparsity at all three layers (from text, Table 1; no row)
source_check.reason: Mean L0 exceeding the 768 input dimensions does not establish dense copying in a 6,144-feature dictionary. The active fractions are 12.6–15.9%; the paper supplies no threshold identifying these results as near-copying, and V4 requires no L0 below the hidden dimension.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Its feature-level structural and RNA-type association results bear directly on V4's dictionary-recoverable-feature claim.

tranche.reason: The study tests dictionary recovery of biologically associated features in a new setting: a frozen RNA language model.

source_check.notes: RNA-type η² values and feature rankings control for length; preferred-type fold enrichments use raw activations. The combined length/composition kNN baseline exceeds both learned representations at layers 0 and 11; only layer 5 exceeds that baseline.

statements.correction: Table 1: mean L0 at layers 0/5/11 = 975/775/791; active fractions of the 6,144-feature dictionary = 15.9%/12.6%/12.9%; hidden dimension = 768. Section 3.1 describes these as sparse representations. No density or copying threshold at L0 = 768 is specified.
statements.problem: The L0 range and hidden dimension are correct, but they do not establish that the recovered representation is dense. The statement inherits an unsupported interpretation from the verdict.
